answer: A bonded reputation registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a refundable deposit and builds a verifiable history of completed jobs, like a jade ledger entry that cannot be copied cheaply. New identities start with low trust and limited access, while a reef of independent attestors checks work before rewards release. Creating thousands of throwaway accounts then costs real deposits and time, and a zephyr of quick, free clones cannot pass the same costly checks, so one real agent earns more than a swarm of fakes.
